newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 2nd quarter life insurance sales up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: French 2nd quarter life insurance sales up 15 pct.

text.p: Contributions to French life insurance companies totalled 113.7 billion francs in the second quarter, up 15 percent from the same period in 1995, according to figures from the French federation of insurance companies (FFSA).

Compared with the first quarter of 1996, contributions fell 15 percent although the FFSA said the large increase in the first quarter, up 28 percent from 1996, had been "atypical". The year-on-year increase for the first half of 1996 was 22 percent.

The FFSA said the slight slowdown in contributions would probably continue in the second half of 1996 an account of a decline in transfers from other savings vehicles combined with a stable French savings rate.
The life insurance figures are based on submissions from 36 insurance companies with a total market share of 84 percent.

A spokeswoman for the FFSA said on Wednesday it was sticking to its forecast for an overall increase of 10 percent in 1996 even though tax relief on contributions to new life insurance policies was abolished on September 5 by Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
"For the moment we're staying with our forecasts," she said.
She declined to comment on the current debate about whether French pension funds should make payouts in annuities or a lump sum.
French banks have pushed for pension funds to pay out money in a lump sum, whereas insurance companies would prefer the payout in the form of annuities.
A draft bill on pension funds drawn up by Finance Minister Jean Arthuis had suggested these should be pay out money in annuities only.
However government officials said on Tuesday the government is to open discussions with interested parties on this issue and lump sum pension fund payments could be considered.
